description: An operations director must authorize a short production run using an alternate polymer resin and finalize the blend, preparation, inspection, and traceability controls, with input from a materials engineer and a regulatory compliance specialist.

shared_context.S1: The normal polymer resin shipment is delayed, while 210 kilograms of the normal resin and 90 kilograms of an alternate resin lot are available in the materials warehouse.
shared_context.S2: The injection-molding line is idle and could produce 600 housings tomorrow if the alternate material is authorized.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision on whether the run may proceed and what controls must be recorded in the production order.
shared_context.S4: The site's pre-run authorization routine requires the operations director to obtain a materials review and a compliance review before releasing a non-routine material run.
shared_context.S5: At the authorization meeting, the materials engineer and compliance specialist each present their formal review findings directly; after both reviews are heard, Elena records the applicable controls and may issue the binding decision without waiting for later confirmations.

PF1.text: Ravi completed a compatibility trial recorded in his lab notebook: the alternate resin is qualified only at exactly 30% alternate resin blended with 70% normal resin, and the combined material must be dried for exactly 4 hours at 80 degrees Celsius; he has not copied the trial result into the production order.

PF2.text: Marta's customer deviation review, based on an approval email not yet entered in the quality system, permits exactly 600 housings from this alternate-resin run, requires exactly 12 first-off units to receive dimensional inspection, and requires serialized lot traceability for every released housing; she must present this formal compliance finding during the authorization meeting.

acceptance_conditions: The alternate-resin run must be authorized.
The blend must contain exactly 30% alternate resin.
The blended material must be dried for exactly 4 hours at 80 degrees Celsius.
Exactly 600 housings may be produced under the customer deviation.
Exactly 12 first-off units must receive dimensional inspection.
Serialized lot traceability must apply to every released housing.
The lab trial and customer deviation must be recorded as commitments and cited in the justification.

content_checks.C7: decisions['alternate_resin_percentage'] == 30 and decisions['drying_hours_at_80C'] == 4 and any('30%' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(('dry' in c['detail'] or 'Dry' in c['detail']) and ('4-hour' in c['detail'] or '4 hours' in c['detail']) and '80' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['production_quantity'] == 600 and decisions['first_off_units_inspected'] == 12 and decisions['serialized_lot_traceability'] == True and any('600' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any('12' in c['detail'] and ('first-off' in c['detail'] or 'first off' in c['detail'] or 'first_off' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) and any('serialized' in c['detail'] or 'Serialized' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The materials plan changes from an unspecified alternate-material run to exactly 30% alternate resin and exactly 4 hours of drying at 80 degrees Celsius, with a material-trial record.
The approved customer deviation changes the run limit to exactly 600 housings, requires exactly 12 inspected first-off units and serialized traceability, and adds a customer-deviation record.
